title: Pitts India Act Of 1784
definition: Enacted by the British Parliament under Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger, the Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a system of double government by distinguishing between the commercial and political functions of the East India Company, placing Indian affairs under the direct control of the British government.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the evolution of British paramountcy in India, the transition from a trading corporation to a territorial sovereign power, and the historical foundation of the dual control system tested frequently in Prelims and Modern Indian History Mains.
learningOutcomes: Master the structural architecture and dual control mechanism introduced by the Pitt's India Act of 1784.
